Subject: POC observability plan & success criteria - FinTechX

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned before the POC kickoff: 

What we heard from FinTechX (agreed goals):
- Validate that Redwood can meet your latency & throughput SLOs for the payments reconciliation flow (target p90 latency < 250ms for generation path).
- Confirm end-to-end observability (tracing, logs, dashboards) so your SREs can triage model fallbacks and token-cost spikes.
- Exercise model fallback & routing policies during simulated load.

Proposed POC scope & timeline:
- 4-week POC starting week of Mar 15, target completion Apr 12.
- Week 0 (prep): networking, API keys, sample prompts, baseline metrics.
- Week 1-2: integration + smoke tests + baseline load.
- Week 3: soak / failure injection (model fallback, region failover).
- Week 4: evaluation, success criteria pass/fail, handoff.

Owners (proposed):
- FinTechX: Priya Shah (Product lead), Zach Patel (Platform / Eng).
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (SE / integration lead), Sean Gallagher (Customer Success).

Action items / asks for FinTechX before kickoff:
1) Confirm success criteria below (see also attachment: poc-success-criteria.xlsx).
2) Provide IP whitelist / VPC peering details or a contact who can configure allowed ingress for our test endpoints.
3) Identify where you want logs/metrics exported (Datadog, Splunk, S3).

Success criteria (draft) — please confirm or edit:
- Performance: p90 generation latency < 250ms for 95% of test cases under expected load profile; no more than 1% model-fallback rate during steady-state tests.
- Observability: dashboards + tracing available with < 1 minute ingestion latency for logs; request-level request_id present in all traces/logs.
- Cost: token cost per reconciliation request within the budget you provided (we’ll compare token counts).

I’ll follow up with a short observability plan from Marissa that details dashboards / traces / metrics we recommend instrumenting for the POC.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

Subject: Observability checklist & dashboard + instrumentation notes (POC)

Hi Priya / Zach —

Attached: redwood-observability-checklist.xlsx and observability-poc-plan.xlsx. Below is a concise plan your SREs/engineers can act on. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

High-level observability plan for FinTechX POC (actionable items):

1) Dashboards (Datadog recommended) — recommended dashboard set and core charts:
- POC — Overview (single pane): total requests, tokens/s, error rate, model-fallback rate, avg/token cost.
- Latency Heatmap: p50/p90/p99 for request and model generation segments.
- Token Cost by Route: tokens per request and estimated $/1000 requests.
- Error Trends & Top error messages by route (sampled logs link).
- Infrastructure: GPU utilization, batch size distribution, queue depth, throughput (tokens/s).

Datadog metric names (suggested labels):
- redwood.request.latency_ms{route,model_version,region}
- redwood.request.generation_latency_ms{route,model_version}
- redwood.request.tokens{route,model_version}
- redwood.request.fallback_count{route,model_version}
- redwood.kv_cache.hit_rate{route}
- redwood.infra.gpu_utilization{host,pool}
- redwood.cost.tokens_usd{route}

2) Tracing
- Correlate traces with request_id and span-level timing for: ingress -> routing -> model_inference -> postprocess.
- Sampling: 100% sampling for first 48 hours of the POC to ensure full traces, then drop to 10% for long-tail monitoring.
- Export: traces to Datadog APM and retain raw spans for 14 days for debugging.

3) Logs & exports
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, request_id, route, user_id (redacted as needed), model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, error_code.
- Export options: push to your S3 bucket (we’ll deliver compressed daily bundles) + optional push to Splunk/Datadog Logs.
- Retention: default 90 days; we can extend if needed (cost delta will be in workbook).

4) Alerts & SLOs (examples)
- Latency SLO breach: p90_generation_latency_ms > 300ms for > 5 minutes -> alert P0 to oncall.
- Model fallback alert: fallback_rate > 2% in a 5m window -> page.
- Token cost spike: tokens_usd change > 3x expected baseline -> notify CS/Cost Engineering.

5) Instrumentation / Integration notes (quick)
- Tokenize at the Redwood SDK boundary; include request_id in all downstream calls.
- Enable prefix/KV cache reporting (we’ll add a header per response with cache_hit boolean).
- If using our private deployment mode, we’ll provide a small agent to forward metrics to your Datadog account; for hosted, we’ll push to your ingestion endpoints.

6) Ownership & access
- Redwood owners: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com) — SE + instrumentation; Sean Gallagher (sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com) — CS / runbook.
- FinTechX owners (please confirm): Priya Shah (product), Zach Patel (platform), Aisha Rahman (SRE).
- Access needs: Datadog API key or a sandbox Datadog board name; S3 bucket ARN + write role; IP whitelist for our test endpoints.

7) Deliverables by 2027-03-12: dashboard JSON for Datadog, instrumentation checklist (attached), evaluation workbook with load profiles (we included this in observability-poc-plan.xlsx).

If this aligns, I’ll upload the Datadog dashboard JSON and the sample alert rules to the shared Drive link and we can schedule a 30-minute handoff.

Thanks — Marissa
